learningObjectives: Translate a project requirement into a modular system architecture.
Design APIs, data storage, services, and application boundaries.
Create a technical implementation plan for the Python capstone.

activities.title: Requirement Map
activities.instruction: Explore how requirements map to system components.

content.concept: System design begins by translating functional and non-functional requirements into components and responsibilities.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Describe what users need the system to accomplish and any important constraints.
Defines how clients communicate with the application through endpoints and request/response contracts.
Coordinates application workflows and use cases.
Contains business rules and core concepts of the application.
Handles persistence and communication with databases or repositories.
Connects the application to external APIs, services, storage, or other systems.

activities.title: System Architecture Builder
activities.instruction: Assemble a modular architecture for the capstone.

content.concept: A modular Python application separates responsibilities so individual components can be developed, tested, and changed with fewer unintended effects.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: API Design Builder
activities.instruction: Compose the essential parts of a REST endpoint.

content.concept: A well-designed API endpoint defines a resource, HTTP operation, path, input contract, and predictable response.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Architecture Decision Selector
activities.instruction: Choose the design decision that best addresses the stated requirement.

content.concept: Architecture decisions should be based on project requirements, constraints, security, maintainability, performance, and expected scale.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Use a repository/data-access layer to isolate database operations
Put all SQL queries directly inside API route functions
Store database passwords directly in source code
Make every module responsible for every application concern
config.answer: Use a repository/data-access layer to isolate database operations
